label: Whatever has its being caused by another is not INFINITE_1
paraphrase: Open bridge, analyst formulation, unattributed. Whatever has its being caused by some other being (CausesIn c x esse for some c other than x) is not INFINITE_1 (not unreceived subsistent being). After ST I q.7 a.2: nothing besides God is infinite absolutely, because anything else has its being received and so limited. It carries the step from caused being to received being, which the typed vocabulary does not connect (INFINITE_1 is an abstract predicate constrained only by sufficient-condition premises such as 'What is its own subsistent being is INFINITE_1'). Scope: CausesIn ... esse is the efficient causing of a distinct effect's being, and the domain individuates beings by their being, so the divine processions are not instances (one being; q.33 a.1 ad 1 uses 'principle', not 'cause'); read with processions as instances of causing being, the bridge would conflict with the case's own Trinitarian commitment that the Son is infinite. Control part 5: without it (both beings infinite), a being with the nine is comprehended by a caused intellect and is not INCOMPREHENSIBLE_2.
